core_obligations: Define omega as the right adjoint applied to the structure sheaf, compare with the relative dualizing complex and show it is a dualizing complex (proof lines 6965-6982).
Read off properties (1), (2), (3) from the vanishing lemma and (4) from the normalisation and the depth criterion (proof lines 6984-6994).
Read off (5) from the description of the adjoint, (6) from the dualizing module lemma and (7) from the smooth proper lemma (proof lines 6996-7008).
proof_roadmap: Definition of omega and dualizingness (proof lines 6965-6982).
difficulty_reason: For a proper scheme X over a field k, the lemma produces a dualizing complex omega with seven listed properties: the cohomology vanishes outside [-dim(X), 0]; omega = H^{-dim(X)} is a coherent (S_2) module supported on the top dimensional components; the support of H^i has dimension at most -i; for closed x the direct sum of the local cohomologies H^i for i in [-i, 0] is nonzero exactly when depth(O_{X,x}) <= -i; there are functorial isomorphisms Ext^i_X(K, omega) = Hom_k(H^{-i}(X, K), k) compatible with shifts and triangles; there are functorial isomorphisms Hom(F, omega) = Hom_k(H^{dim(X)}(X, F), k); and for X smooth of relative dimension d over k one has omega = wedge^d Omega_{X/k}[d] up to isomorphism (statement lines 6933-6963). The proof takes omega = a(O_{Spec(k)}) for the right adjoint a of the structure morphism f : X -> Spec(k) from Lemma labelled lemma-twisted-inverse-image, compares it with the relative dualizing complex of Remark labelled remark-relative-dualizing-complex, and uses f proper to identify it with f^!O_{Spec(k)} and Lemma labelled lemma-shriek-dualizing to see that it is a dualizing complex, matching the Examples labelled example-proper-over-local and example-equidimensional-over-field (proof lines 6965-6982). Parts (1), (2) and (3) come from Lemma labelled lemma-vanishing-good-dualizing; part (4) from Lemma labelled lemma-good-dualizing-normalized together with Dualizing Complexes, Lemma labelled dualizing-lemma-depth-in-terms-dualizing-complex; part (5) from the identification of a with the right adjoint of K -> RGamma(X, K) and of D(k) with graded k-vector spaces; part (6) from Lemma labelled lemma-dualizing-module-proper-over-A, with the general case by unwinding (5); and part (7) from Lemma labelled lemma-smooth-proper (proof lines 6984-7008). Recognising that the right adjoint of the structure morphism is precisely the object whose seven properties are then read off the cited structural results is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2.
